gloss: be apart, alone; a part; alone, besides; (homographs) pole, linen, empty talk
summary: The root is being apart from others. Its commonest word, בַּד, is a part taken by itself: with לְ, לְבַד is “alone, by itself, only” (Gen 2:18; Deu 8:3), and with מִן, מִלְּבַד is “besides, over and above”, as the feast offerings of Lev 23 are over and above the sabbaths of Yahweh and the people’s own gifts (Lev 23:38). בָּדָד is dwelling apart, the leper’s isolation (Lev 13:46), Israel’s security as a people alone (Num 23:9; Deu 33:28), and the desolation of a forsaken city (Lam 1:1); Yahweh alone is God, with none beside him (Deu 4:35; Deu 32:12; 2Ki 19:15). The same spelling is the carrying poles of the ark and altars and the limbs and branches that stand out from a body or a vine, the priests’ linen, and the empty talk of boasters, whose ties to the root are less clear. Arabic badda “separate”, istabadda “be alone” and budd “a portion” share the root’s sense.

words.gloss: a part; (לְבַד) alone, by itself, only; (מִלְּבַד) besides; pole, limb, branch
words.summary: A part, one taken apart from the rest. Alone it is used of portions and of the parts that stand out from a thing: the poles that carry the ark and altars, the limbs of a body, the branches of a vine. Nearly all its uses are with a preposition: לְבַד “by itself, alone, only” and מִלְּבַד “apart from, besides”, the commonest words of scripture for “alone” and “besides”.

senses.definition: With לְ and usually a suffix: by itself, with no one else; and so “only”, the one and none other.

evidence.note: “It is not good that the man should be לְבַדּוֹ; I will make him a helper fit for him”: alone, without another of his kind.
Jethro: “Why do you sit לְבַדֶּךָ, and all the people stand by you from morning to evening?”
“You are not able to do it לְבַדֶּךָ.”
Moses: “I am not able to bear all this people לְבַדִּי, for it is too heavy for me.”
“And Jacob was left לְבַדּוֹ, and a man wrestled with him.”
“His brother is dead, and he alone is left.”
Joseph is served by himself, his brothers by themselves, the Egyptians by themselves: apart, each company on its own.
Eglon sitting in his cool upper room alone.
Elijah: “I, I alone (לְבַדִּי), am left, and they seek my life”; again 1Ki 19:14. Paul quotes it, “κἀγὼ ὑπελείφθην μόνος” (Rom 11:3).
Quoting 1Ki 19:10: “I am left alone (μόνος).”
“I alone have escaped to tell you”; also Job 1:16, 17, 19.
“Man does not live on bread לְבַדּוֹ, but on everything that comes out of the mouth of Yahweh does man live”: only, and nothing more.
Jesus quotes Deu 8:3: “οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ”; also Luk 4:4.
“Against you, you only (לְבַדְּךָ), have I sinned”; the verse’s second half is quoted in Rom 3:4.
“If you scoff, you alone shall bear it.”
“Let them be yours alone, and not strangers’ with you.”
Though Noah, Daniel and Job were in it, “they only would be delivered”; also Ezk 14:18.
Those who join house to house “until you are made to dwell alone in the midst of the land”.
“I have trodden the winepress alone (לְבַדִּי), and of the peoples there was no man with me.”
“I Daniel alone saw the vision; the men with me did not see it”; also Dan 10:8.
“Only (לְבַד) this have I found: that God made man upright, but they have sought out many devices.”
Death for whoever goes in uncalled, “except (לְבַד) the one to whom the king holds out the golden sceptre”.

senses.gloss: (of God) alone, he and no other
senses.definition: Of Yahweh: he alone is God, and he alone does what only God does; there is no other beside him.

evidence.note: “To you it was shown, that you might know that Yahweh, he is God; there is none else מִלְבַדּוֹ, besides him.”
Hezekiah: “You are the God, you alone (לְבַדְּךָ), of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made the heavens and the earth”; also Isa 37:16.
“That all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are Yahweh God, you alone”; also Isa 37:20.
“You are Yahweh, you alone; you have made the heavens, the heaven of heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is on it.”
“I am Yahweh who makes all things, who stretches out the heavens alone (לְבַדִּי), who spreads out the earth by myself.”
“Who alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.”
“You are great and do wondrous things; you are God alone.”
“That they may know that you, whose name alone is Yahweh, are the Most High over all the earth.”
“Who alone does wondrous things”; also Psa 136:4.
“His name alone is exalted.”
“Yahweh alone shall be exalted in that day”; also Isa 2:17.
“Put away the foreign gods … and serve him only (לְבַדּוֹ)”; and Israel served Yahweh only (1Sa 7:4).
“I will make mention of your righteousness, yours alone.”

senses.gloss: (מִלְּבַד, לְבַד מִן) besides, over and above, apart from
senses.definition: With מִן, or followed by it: apart from, not counting; so “besides, in addition to”, of what is reckoned over and above something else.

evidence.note: The feast offerings are “מִלְּבַד the sabbaths of Yahweh, and מִלְּבַד your gifts, and מִלְּבַד all your vows, and מִלְּבַד all your freewill offerings”: over and above them, not in their place.
“These you shall offer to Yahweh at your appointed times, לְבַד מִנִּדְרֵיכֶם, besides your vows and your freewill offerings.”
The Passover offerings “מִלְּבַד the burnt offering of the morning, which is for a continual burnt offering”: the daily offering goes on beside them. So for each feast, Num 28:31; 29:6, 11, 16 to 38.
The grain offering burned “besides the burnt offering of the morning”.
About six hundred thousand men on foot, “לְבַד מִטָּף”, not counting the children.
All the souls who came with Jacob into Egypt, “besides Jacob’s sons’ wives”.
A famine “besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham”.
The Levite shall eat a like portion, “besides what comes from the sale of his patrimony”.
The words of the covenant in Moab, “besides the covenant he made with them in Horeb”.
To build no altar “besides the altar of Yahweh our God that is before his dwelling”.
“Other lords besides you have ruled over us; by you only we make mention of your name.”
All the sons of David, “besides the sons of the concubines”.
The congregation numbered “besides their servants and their maids”; also Neh 7:67.

senses.gloss: a part; (בַּד בְּבַד) part for part, equally; (לְבָד) by themselves
senses.definition: A portion taken apart from others: in the phrase בַּד בְּבַד, each part matched by a part, in equal measure; and of things set in groups apart from each other.

evidence.note: The spices of the incense: “בַּד בְּבַד shall it be”, a part for a part, each in equal measure.
“You shall couple five curtains לְבָד and six curtains לְבָד”: each set by itself; also Exo 36:16.
Jacob set his own flocks by themselves, and did not put them with Laban’s.
Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves; also Gen 21:29.
“The land shall mourn, every family apart (לְבָד): the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart”; through Zec 12:14.
“Everyone who laps the water with his tongue … you shall set him by himself.”

senses.definition: A part that stands out from the whole: the carrying poles set through the rings of the ark, the table and the altars; the limbs of a body; the branches of a vine; and the bars of a gate.

evidence.note: “You shall make בַדֵּי of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, and put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark with them” (Exo 25:13–14).
“The poles shall be in the rings of the ark; they shall not be taken from it.”
The table’s rings, “as holders for the poles to carry the table”; also Exo 25:28.
The poles of the altar of burnt offering, overlaid with bronze; Exo 27:7.
The incense altar’s rings, “holders for the poles to carry it with”; Exo 30:5.
At the breaking of camp the Kohathites cover the ark and “put in its poles”; also Num 4:8, 11, 14.
In Solomon’s house “the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place before the inner sanctuary, but they were not seen outside”; also 2Ch 5:9.
The cherubim covered the ark and its poles above; also 2Ch 5:8.
“It shall devour the בַּדֵּי of his skin; the firstborn of death shall devour his בַּדָּיו”: the members of his body.
“I will not keep silent about his בַּדָּיו, nor his mighty strength”: the limbs of Leviathan.
The vine “made בַּדִּים and sent out shoots”: branches.
“Fire has gone out from a rod of her branches (בַּדֶּיהָ); it has devoured her fruit.”
“They shall go down to the בַּדֵּי of the grave”: the bars of Sheol, as of a gate shut on the dead.
“The sword shall whirl in his cities and consume his בַּדָּיו”: beside “his cities”, likely the bars of their gates; but the word could be read as the empty talkers of Isa 44:25.

evidence.locator: Gen.2.18, לְבַדּוֹ → μόνον; 2Ki.19.15, 19, Neh.9.6, Psa.86.10, Isa.44.24 → μόνος; μόνος renders בַּד ×53

evidence.note: “Man shall not live by bread alone (μόνῳ)”, quoting Deu 8:3, לְבַדּוֹ.
“I am left alone (μόνος)”, quoting Elijah, 1Ki 19:10, לְבַדִּי.
“That they may know you, the only (μόνον) true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent.”
“For you alone (μόνος) are holy.”

evidence.locator: Num.29.39, לְבַד → πλήν; πλήν renders בַּד ×7

evidence.note: The scribe: “there is one God, and there is none other but him (πλὴν αὐτοῦ)”, the confession of Deu 4:35, אֵין עוֹד מִלְבַדּוֹ.

parallels.note: “There is none else”, beside מִלְבַדּוֹ of Yahweh.

opposites.note: “A helper fit for him”, the answer to the man’s being לְבַדּוֹ.

phrases.gloss: part for part, in equal measure

words.gloss: alone, apart, in isolation; in security
words.summary: Apart from others, mostly of dwelling or sitting so: the leper outside the camp, Israel apart from the nations and safe, a city emptied of its people, a man alone in grief. Whether that apartness is safety or desolation depends on whether Yahweh is with the one apart.

senses.definition: Living or sitting apart from others, cut off from company: of the unclean put out of the camp, of a forsaken city, and of one in grief.

evidence.note: The leper: “He is unclean; בָּדָד he shall dwell; outside the camp shall his dwelling be.”
“How the city sits בָדָד that was full of people! She has become like a widow.”
“The fortified city is בָּדָד, a habitation forsaken and left like the wilderness.”
“Let him sit alone and keep silent, because he has laid it on him.”
“I did not sit in the company of the merrymakers … I sat alone because of your hand, for you filled me with indignation.”

senses.definition: Living apart from others with nothing to fear: a people needing no walls or alliances, for none is near to threaten them.

evidence.note: Balaam: “Behold, a people that dwells לְבָדָד, and does not reckon itself among the nations.”
“Israel dwells in safety, בָּדָד, the fountain of Jacob, in a land of grain and new wine.”
Hazor: “a nation at ease that dwells securely … that has neither gates nor bars, that dwells alone.”
“Shepherd your people with your rod, the flock of your inheritance, dwelling alone in the forest in the midst of Carmel.”
“In peace I will both lie down and sleep, for you, Yahweh, לְבָדָד, make me dwell in safety”: alone, or “in security apart”.

senses.definition: Of Yahweh acting with no other god beside him.

evidence.note: “Yahweh בָּדָד led him, and there was no foreign god with him.”

evidence.locator: Num.23.9, בָדָד → μόνος; Deu.33.28 the same; μόνος renders בָּדָד ×4

parallels.note: “And no foreign god with him”, the meaning of Yahweh’s leading בָּדָד.

opposites.note: “Full of people”, what the city was before it sat alone.

words.summary: Only the qal participle בּוֹדֵד, three times, of one apart from its fellows: a straggler out of the ranks, a wild ass alone, a bird alone on a roof.

senses.gloss: be alone, apart from one’s fellows
senses.definition: Of a creature or a man on its own, away from the others of its kind.

evidence.note: “I watch, and have become like a sparrow בּוֹדֵד on the housetop”: the afflicted man without friend or comfort.
“They have gone up to Assyria, a wild ass בּוֹדֵד לוֹ, alone by himself”: Ephraim wandering off on its own to hire lovers.
Smoke comes from the north, “and there is no בּוֹדֵד in his ranks”: none falling out alone, the army coming in unbroken order.

words.summary: The linen of the priests’ garments, and of the man clothed in linen in Ezekiel and Daniel. How it comes from the root of separation is not known: nothing in scripture or the cognates ties it to “part, alone”, and it may be another word in the same spelling (see the entry’s note).

senses.definition: The cloth of the priests’ undergarments and of the high priest’s garments on the day of coverings: linen, made of fine twined שֵׁשׁ.

evidence.note: “The linen breeches (מִכְנְסֵי הַבָּד) of fine twined linen (שֵׁשׁ מָשְׁזָר)”: the בַּד garment made of שֵׁשׁ.
“Linen breeches (מִכְנְסֵי־בָד) to cover the flesh of their nakedness, from the loins to the thighs.”
On the day of coverings the high priest puts on “the holy linen coat, the linen breeches, the linen sash and the linen turban; these are holy garments”.
He takes off the linen garments when he comes out of the holy place; also Lev 16:32.
The priest puts on “his linen garment (מִדּוֹ בַד) and linen breeches” to take up the ashes of the altar.
“Samuel ministered before Yahweh, a boy girded with a linen ephod.”
Doeg kills eighty-five men “who wore a linen ephod”: priests.
David danced before Yahweh “girded with a linen ephod”; also 1Ch 15:27 with בּוּץ.

senses.gloss: (clothed in) linen, of a messenger from God
senses.definition: The dress of the man in Ezekiel’s and Daniel’s visions who marks, judges and reveals, clothed as a priest.

evidence.note: Among the six men with weapons, “one man clothed in linen (לָבֻשׁ בַּדִּים), with a writer’s inkhorn at his side”, who marks the foreheads of those who sigh (Ezk 9:4).
The man clothed in linen reports, “I have done as you commanded me.”
He takes coals of fire from between the cherubim; also Ezk 10:6, 7.
“A man clothed in linen (לָבוּשׁ בַּדִּים), his loins girded with gold of Uphaz”, his face as lightning and eyes as torches of fire.
“How long to the end of these wonders?” asked of the man clothed in linen; also Dan 12:7.

evidence.locator: Ezk.9.2, בַּדִּים → ποδήρη; ποδήρης renders בַּד ×3

evidence.note: One like the son of man “clothed with a garment down to the foot (ποδήρη), and girded about the breasts with a golden girdle”, with eyes as a flame of fire and feet like bronze (Rev 1:14–15): Daniel’s man clothed in linen (Dan 10:5–6), in the Septuagint’s word for Ezekiel’s.

evidence.locator: Dan.10.5, בַּדִּים → βύσσινα; βύσσινος renders בַּד ×4

evidence.note: The bride is given “to be clothed in fine linen (βύσσινον), clean and white; for the fine linen is the righteousness of the saints”.
The armies in heaven follow him “clothed in fine linen, white and clean”.

parallels.note: Fine linen, the stuff the בַּד breeches are made of.

words.summary: Talk made up out of one’s own heart, with nothing behind it: the boasting of Moab and of Job’s friend, and in the plural the talkers who give such speech out as signs. It goes with the verb בָּדָא, “invent”, and Syriac bdā “feign”, more than with the root’s sense of being apart; how the two meet is not clear.

senses.definition: Words that claim more than is so; boasts with no truth or deed behind them.

evidence.note: “We have heard of the pride of Moab … his pride and his arrogance and his wrath; his בַּדָּיו are not so”: his boasts are not true.
“I know his wrath, says Yahweh, that it is not so; his בַּדָּיו have done not so”: boasts not matched by deeds.
Zophar to Job: “Should your בַּדֶּיךָ make men hold their peace? And when you mock, shall no one make you ashamed?”

senses.definition: Those whose words are invented: men who give out signs and counsel that Yahweh brings to nothing.

evidence.note: Yahweh “frustrates the signs of the בַּדִּים and makes diviners (קֹסְמִים) mad, turns the wise backward and makes their knowledge foolish”.
“A sword is upon the בַּדִּים, and they shall become fools”: among Babylon’s princes and wise men (Jer 50:35).

parallels.note: Diviners, beside the בַּדִּים whose signs Yahweh frustrates.
Pride, of which Moab’s boasts are the voice.

words.gloss: invent, devise (out of one’s own heart)
words.summary: Twice, both times of what someone made up from his own heart with no word of God or fact behind it. Its spelling differs from the root’s; it is kept here with the noun בַּד “empty talk”, which shares its meaning.

senses.gloss: invent, devise from one’s own heart
senses.definition: Make something up out of oneself: a feast no law appointed, a charge with no fact behind it.

evidence.note: Jeroboam offered at Bethel “in the month which he had devised from his own heart (אֲשֶׁר־בָּדָא מִלִּבּוֹ)”, a feast to rival the feast in Judah (1Ki 12:32).
Nehemiah to Sanballat: “No such things are done as you say, for you invent them (בוֹדָאם) out of your own heart.”
False teachers “with feigned (πλαστοῖς) words make merchandise of you”, the adjective of πλάσσω; the Peshitta has the same root’s bēdyā here (see בֵּדְיָא).

words.summary: The Peshitta’s word for the “feigned” words of false teachers: speech made up to deceive.

senses.definition: Words invented to deceive, with nothing true behind them.

evidence.note: “Through covetousness they shall make merchandise of you with words of bēdyā”, for the Greek πλαστοῖς λόγοις, “feigned words”: the false teachers of 2Pe 2:1.

cognates.gloss: separate, disperse; (X istabadda) be alone, independent of others; budd, bidād a lot, portion, share
cognates.note: Every part of the Hebrew is here: the verb “separate”, form X “be alone, with none to share with him”, the noun a portion set apart (בַּד “a part”), and form IV giving to each his share singly, as בַּד בְּבַד is part for part. The phrase لَا بُدَّ “there is no separating oneself from it” is the common Arabic “necessarily”.

evidence.note: “He separated, disunited, dispersed, or dissipated; … as also بَدَّ”.
“He was, or became, alone; independent of others; … exclusively of others; without any to share, or participate, with him”.
“A lot, share, portion, or set portion; of anything”; بِدَّة “a piece, or portion, separated, disunited, or dispersed”.
“He divided among them the gift, giving to each of them his lot, or share, or portion, singly”.

cognates.note: Listed in the Proto-Semitic root sets with Arabic badda and Hebrew בָּדַד; not yet checked in a Ge'ez dictionary.

evidence.locator: SEM000009 bdd [separate] V; GEZ000956 bdd [separate] V

cognates.note: The same verb as בָּדָא, “invent”, with its noun of invented or empty speech, as בַּד “empty talk”. Its noun is used in the Peshitta (2Pe 2:3), recorded as a word of the entry.
The Jerusalem Targum renders Moses’ “I have not done them of my own heart” (Num 16:28) with this verb: invent, make up.

evidence.note: “to invent. Targ. Y. II. Num. XVI, 28 בְּדֵית (Var. בָּדִית).”

doctrine.statement: Israel was shown Yahweh’s works “that you might know that Yahweh, he is God; there is none else besides him (מִלְבַדּוֹ)” (Deu 4:35), and “Yahweh alone (בָּדָד) led him, and there was no foreign god with him” (Deu 32:12). Hezekiah prays, “you are the God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made the heavens and the earth”, that all may know “you are Yahweh God, you alone” (2Ki 19:15, 19); the Levites, “you are Yahweh, you alone; you have made the heavens … the earth and all that is on it” (Neh 9:6); and Yahweh says, “I am Yahweh who makes all things, who stretches out the heavens alone, who spreads out the earth by myself” (Isa 44:24). In the New Testament the scribe answers Jesus, “there is one God, and there is none other but him”, in the words of Deu 4:35, and Jesus says he answered wisely (Mrk 12:32–34); Jesus himself, praying to the Father, calls him “the only true God” and himself “Jesus Christ whom you have sent” (Jhn 17:3); and Paul writes, “to us there is one God, the Father, of whom are all things … and one Lord Jesus Christ” (1Co 8:6). From the verses: Yahweh alone is God, and he alone made the heavens and the earth, with no one beside him; the Son is the one he sent, named by Jesus himself apart from “the only true God”, not a second God beside him.

Balaam, looking on Israel from the rocks, says, “Behold, a people that dwells alone, and does not reckon itself among the nations” (Num 23:9); Moses blesses them, “Israel dwells in safety, alone, the fountain of Jacob” (Deu 33:28), with “there is none like the God of Jeshurun … the eternal God is your refuge” (Deu 33:26–27); and the song says why: “Yahweh alone led him, and there was no foreign god with him” (Deu 32:12). Micah asks Yahweh to shepherd “the flock of your inheritance, dwelling alone” (Mic 7:14). But when Jerusalem forsook him, the same word described her ruin: “how the city sits alone that was full of people; she has become like a widow” (Lam 1:1), as the leper unclean “shall dwell alone outside the camp” (Lev 13:46). From the verses: Israel’s apartness from the nations was its safety while Yahweh alone was with it; apart from him, to be alone is desolation.

note: Root key בדד as the corpus keys it. Linen בַּד (b.ae.ak) is filed in the database under root בגד by BDB’s page order; it is spelled בד and kept here. Its tie to the root is unexplained: Egyptian bḏꜣ “stiff roll of linen (med.); cloth splint, pad” (TLA tla58590, Wb 1, 488.13) has been proposed as its source, but that is a medical term and the sound match (Egyptian ḏ to Hebrew ד) is not checked; recorded here, not as a cognate. The Mishnah’s play that בַּד is flax growing “stalk by stalk” is a later explanation, not evidence. Poles, limbs and branches are kept as a sense of בַּד “part” under BDB’s one key (b.af.ab); they could be a separate homograph. Hos 11:6 בַּדָּיו is read as bars, but could be “empty talkers”. The idle-talk noun (b.ag.ab, with BDB’s root head b.ag.aa) and the verb בָּדָא (b.ae.am, root בדא) are kept together here; if a separate בדא entry is ever written, move בָּדָא and the Syriac בֵּדְיָא there. Token counts overlap: the database files every בַּדִּים/בַּדָּיו under all three בַּד keys by spelling. Left out: בְּדֵי (b.ag.ad) belongs to דַּי; the names Bedad (b.ag.ac, Gen 36:35) and Bedeiah (b.ag.ae, Ezr 10:35) have no name entries yet. Ge'ez bdd is only from the Proto-Semitic root list; check Dillmann or Leslau. Klein’s Jewish Aramaic בַּדָּא “pole” and Arabic badd “olive press” not followed. Akkadian buddudu “squander” (Oracc armep/x000052910) matches Arabic baddada “dissipate” rather than any Hebrew sense; left out.
